name: io.github.imran0786/tiktok-scripts
title: TikTok Scripts | InayaFlow
description: Public TikTok data for creators: scripts and hooks from top videos, niche trends, posting times.

tools.name: get_tiktok_script_and_hook_inputs
tools.description: Use this when someone asks for a TikTok script, a viral TikTok script, hooks or opening lines, a caption, a title, or video and content ideas for a specific public TikTok account. Input: the TikTok username. It reads that account’s recent public videos and returns the ones with the most views (up to 5) and the ones with the fewest, each with how it compares to the account’s typical (median) views, their captions and opening lines, the hashtags used and the posting rhythm, plus a writing method with 7 hook types. When the niche is clear from the captions, it adds a few recent public posts from other creators in that niche (a stored weekly sample). The scripts, hooks, captions or ideas are then written from this data. Public data only: it cannot read private accounts, watch time or the words spoken inside a video. It does not predict or promise views.

username.description: Required. The public TikTok username to read, as text, with or without @ (for example nasa), or a tiktok.com profile link.

tools.name: get_tiktok_niche_trends
tools.description: Use this when someone asks what is trending or working in a TikTok niche this week, or wants ideas based on what a niche is posting now. Input: a niche or topic in plain words (for example skincare, gym, TikTok Shop finds, personal finance). Returns the stored public posts with the most views from the last 7 days (14 or 30 days, or the wider niche, when there are too few; it says which), each with its opening line, caption, hashtags, views, date and TikTok link, plus counts of the hashtags and opening styles they share. It reads a stored sample that is refreshed weekly: it looks nothing up on TikTok, is not TikTok’s own trending list, and does not predict or promise views.

niche.description: The niche, sub-niche or topic in plain words, for example skincare, gym, TikTok Shop finds or personal finance. Text.

username.description: Optional. A public TikTok username, used only when no niche is given and that account was already read in the last 24 hours: the niche is then taken from its captions. Nothing is looked up on TikTok.

tools.name: get_tiktok_posting_times
tools.description: Use this when someone asks for the best time to post on TikTok for their account, or when a specific public TikTok account should post. Input: the TikTok username, and optionally the creator’s time zone. It reads the account’s recent public videos and returns, for each 3-hour window and each weekday in which the account posted, how many videos were posted and their median views against the account’s typical views, plus the window with the highest median when at least two windows hold 2 or more videos. When the niche is clear from the captions, it adds when other creators’ stored posts in that niche were posted, as a secondary signal. It only compares past posting times with public view counts: it cannot see when followers are online, and a few videos are a weak signal. It does not predict or promise views.

username.description: Required. The public TikTok username to read, as text, with or without @ (for example nasa), or a tiktok.com profile link.

time_zone.description: Optional. The creator’s time zone as an IANA name, for example America/New_York. Leave out to use UTC. Text.

tools.name: get_tiktok_trending_hashtags
tools.description: Use this when someone asks for trending TikTok hashtags, or which hashtags to use, for a niche or topic. Input: a niche or topic in plain words (for example skincare, gym, meal prep). Returns the hashtags used by 2 or more stored public posts from 2 or more creators in that niche over the last 7 days (14 or 30 days, or the wider niche, when there are too few; it says which), with how many posts and creators used each, the median views of those posts and a link to an example post. It reads a stored sample that is refreshed weekly: it looks nothing up on TikTok, is not TikTok’s own trending list, and hashtags do not promise reach.

niche.description: The niche, sub-niche or topic in plain words, for example skincare, gym, TikTok Shop finds or personal finance. Text.

username.description: Optional. A public TikTok username, used only when no niche is given and that account was already read in the last 24 hours: the niche is then taken from its captions. Nothing is looked up on TikTok.

tools.name: check_tiktok_account
tools.description: Use this when someone asks to analyze, check or review a public TikTok account, or how an account is doing. Input: the TikTok username. Returns followers, following, total likes, number of videos, typical (median) views, engagement rate from the recent public videos, the strongest and weakest recent videos (up to 3 each), counted patterns (videos above typical, hashtags used, how the opening lines start) and how often the account posts. Public data only: it cannot see private accounts, watch time, audience details or earnings.

username.description: Required. The public TikTok username to read, as text, with or without @ (for example nasa), or a tiktok.com profile link.

tools.name: get_tiktok_growth_plan
tools.description: Use this when someone asks how to grow on TikTok, how to get more views or followers, or how to go viral on TikTok, for a specific public TikTok account. Input: the TikTok username, and optionally the creator’s time zone and niche. It reads the account once and returns, in one result, the account’s numbers with its strongest and weakest recent videos and counted patterns, its past posting times against views, a few stored public posts and hashtags from its niche when the niche is known, and a method for laying these out as a plan of things to test. Public data only: it cannot see when followers are online, watch time or audience details. It is a plan to test: it does not predict or promise views, followers or any result.

username.description: Required. The public TikTok username to read, as text, with or without @ (for example nasa), or a tiktok.com profile link.

time_zone.description: Optional. The creator’s time zone as an IANA name, for example America/New_York. Leave out to use UTC. Text.

niche.description: Optional. The account’s niche in plain words, for example skincare or gym. Leave out to take it from the captions. Text.

tools.name: check_tiktok_view_drop
tools.description: Use this when someone asks why their TikTok views dropped, or whether the views of a public TikTok account have gone down. Input: the TikTok username. It compares the median views of the 5 newest public videos that are at least 3 days old with the median of the videos before them and says whether that is a big drop (under half of usual). The result keeps what was observed apart from possible causes: the causes are general possibilities to check, not findings. Videos from the last 3 days are left out because they are still collecting views. It only compares public view counts: it cannot see TikTok’s internal account status and does not confirm any restriction. It needs at least 8 public videos that are 3 days old or older.

username.description: Required. The public TikTok username to read, as text, with or without @ (for example nasa), or a tiktok.com profile link.
